 KAMAL KUMAR ARORA
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The categoric stand of the petitioner is that there was a violation of mandatory requirement in terms of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, inasmuch as that the petitioner was never given option for re-testing of the second sample before the Central Laboratory at Mysore.
The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner for the first time was noticed in the order dated 06.12.2017 and following order was passed.

"The contention of the petitioner is that the provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been complied with and also that the criminal complaint is pending since last 17 years without having examined any of the prosecution witness.
Learned Government Advocate for the respondent-State is directed to seek instructions as to whether compliance has been made or not?
If made, provide copy of the intimation or analysis report given to the complainant.

sentences.text: If on the next date of hearing, the same is not produced, the Court would be constrained to pass order of staying the further proceeding of the criminal complaint case pending before the trial Court.
Case be listed on 13.12.2017."
During the intervening period, the case was also dismissed for non-prosecution on 10.08.2023, but the same was restored vide order dated 30.01.2024.

On number of occasions, even last opportunity was granted to the learned State counsel to submit the report in respect of compliance of provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Till date, the compliance has not been made.
The inaction on behalf of the State has unnecessarily consumed valuable time of the Court for nothing.
The stand of the petitioner in respect of non compliance of provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act has not been denied till date and the same amounts to admission.
Virtually, the case has gone uncontested by the State.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State has been involved only in seeking unnecessary adjournments from time to time and has not taken any steps to produce the relevant material to show that the compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, was ever made.
In view of aforesaid, this Court has no alternative, but to accept the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner.

The compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was repaired to be mandatorily done and non-compliance of the same would result in discarding the prosecution story against the petitioner.
As a result of the aforesaid, this petition is accepted.
The impugned prosecution against the petitioner is quashed.

(RAJ MOHAN SINGH) JUDGE b Kamal Kumar Arora vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 22 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191912589/
